clue.text: Kinky practices with an individual who might get you dreaming

definitions.text: individual who might get you dreaming

parts.note: S and M, short for sadomasochism
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone into kinky games who also promises sweet dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: S and M is written out in full as S-AND-M, then the clue's own word is tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore the Sandman sprinkles sand in children's eyes to send them off to sleep.

clue.text: First husband has terrible tan fixed

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man and Eve's husband

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the following letters are mangled into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The first husband is stuck with an awful suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant holds an unshakeable position, set firmly and immovably in their opinion.

clue.text: Uneducated type in drably coloured church …

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An ignorant figure sits in a drab grey church, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow learner, traditionally a schoolchild made to wear a pointed cap.

clue.text: … claims every side's lacking depth

parts.note: every one is all

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken out of what comes before

parts.note: sides are edges
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Continuing the dunce: he says every side lacks depth.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL EDGES loses its D to leave ALLEGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something as true without proof, which is to make a claim.

clue.text: Brought down drone that's exhausted

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
bled as in drained, used up

explanation.surface: A military drone that has run out of power is shot down.
explanation.walkthrough: Drone looks like the flying machine, but here it is the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbled means lowered in pride or status, taken down a peg.

clue.text: Central fund issues currency when confidence is lacking

indicators.note: central asks for the letters at the very middle of each following word

parts.note: middle two of four letters
middle two of six letters
middle two of eight letters

explanation.surface: A central bank fund prints money at a time when confidence in the economy has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsure is a state of doubt, describing someone at a moment of hesitation and uncertainty.

clue.text: Curse, as sheep and lamb go astray

indicators.note: things that go astray wander off course, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two fodder words

explanation.surface: A shepherd swears as the flock wanders off.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely or irreverently, swearing using sacred names.

clue.text: Criminal dealer acquires minute stone

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other
a criminal version is a corrupt, bent one, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A crooked fence gets hold of a tiny gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute looks like 'tiny' describing the stone, but it is the time unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gem, a variety of beryl.

clue.text: Hard drug has edge, but you won't react with it

parts.note: stiff means rigid, hard
an upper is a stimulant drug
the lip of a cup is its edge

explanation.surface: A hard drug has an edge to it, yet leaves you unresponsive.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a stiff upper lip means showing no emotion in adversity, the famous British reserve.

clue.text: Regulars leave drab wine when night is over

indicators.note: letters at regular intervals drop out, so only every other one stays

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Pub regulars walk out on dull wine as the late night ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Regulars sounds like pub customers, but means letters at regular spacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, the first light that comes as darkness ends.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker set out real alternative

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hedonist lays out what a real alternative lifestyle looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a fruit that left them in idle, dreamy contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotus-eater is someone who lives a life of indolent indulgence, idly chasing enjoyment.

clue.text: Incomparable lady from South Pacific

parts.note: surface reading: a peerless woman from an island in the Pacific
setter's reading: the musical South Pacific has the song There Is Nothing Like a ..., naming a lady with no equal

explanation.walkthrough: South Pacific is the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, not the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The title word of the sailors' song is a woman, here one beyond comparison because nothing is like her.

clue.text: Wrap frayed rope in skin — it makes it last longer

indicators.note: to wrap one thing in another is to put it inside a covering

parts.note: to flay is to strip off the skin

indicators.note: a frayed thing has come apart at the ends, so its letters unravel into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for preserving a worn rope by sheathing it in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'it' is the rope; the cheeky reading makes 'it' the act of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreplay is the sexual activity before intercourse, said to prolong the encounter.

clue.text: As it is, half of stations used quotas

indicators.note: half of asks for only the front part of each following word

parts.note: first four of eight letters
first two of four letters
first three of six letters

explanation.surface: A report that half the stations are meeting their quotas as things stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Status quo is Latin for the existing state of affairs, things left unchanged.

clue.text: Doctor seals test? That's improper

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with sealed exam papers, which is out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless behaviour is vulgar or offensive, lacking decorum and propriety.

clue.text: Exciting call for attention when receiving bill

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: hey! calls for someone's attention
a bill posted on a wall is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A thrilling shout of 'oi!' as someone is handed the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means intoxicating or exhilarating, sweeping someone off their feet.

clue.text: Newly made retreat for high end personal servant

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to a lord

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A posh holiday retreat staffed with a personal butler.
explanation.walkthrough: High end looks like 'upmarket', but it splits: end of high.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh food or bread is recently produced, not stale.

clue.text: Come across crash …

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both bumping into an acquaintance and colliding with a vehicle or obstacle.

clue.text: Society relaxed about summit where dodgy booze was served

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
easy means relaxed, at ease
a summit is a peak

explanation.surface: A laid-back club relaxing around a mountain top bar selling illicit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The container sits inside the second half of the charade, not around the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was an illicit bar selling alcohol during American Prohibition.

clue.text: … feeling excited, investigating learner's part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the words, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Following on from the crash: a learner driver is thrilled to be investigating it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be atingle is to be tingling with anticipation, thrilled and quivering.

clue.text: Cheat swapping spades for diamonds in contract

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means one letter is put in place of a different one

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, which is replaced
to contract is to shrink or dwindle

explanation.surface: A bridge cheat switches suits in his contract.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like the bridge bid, but it is a verb meaning shrink; DWINDLE has its D replaced by S.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle is to defraud someone, obtaining money by deception.

clue.text: Diner where writer holds empty seat

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a trademark used generically in Britain

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A restaurant where an author keeps a seat free.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant, a place to eat; diner here is the eatery, not the customer.

clue.text: Bury stores port for country's central region

indicators.note: something that stores another holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to inter is to bury
Rio de Janeiro is a famous port

explanation.surface: Burying the port wine supply in the heart of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior of a country is its inland heartland, away from the coasts.

clue.text: Purchase tops for girl resplendent in pink

indicators.note: the tops of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters

explanation.surface: Shopping for tops for a girl who looks great in pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase looks like buying, but here it is the noun for a firm grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a secure grasp or leverage, as when a climber finds a foothold in rock.

clue.text: Doctor interrupted by peculiar surly type

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A doctor is interrupted by a strange, bad-tempered patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A grump is an irritable, grouchy person, always grumbling.

clue.text: Taking colonists away is bothersome

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read whimsically: undoing the settling of a place

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful split: settlers removed is un-settling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsettling disturbs or upsets, making people anxious and uneasy.

clue.text: Language spoken at that cockney woman's party?

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the answer is a sound-alike of the words

parts.note: a cockney drops the h of her, and a do is a party

explanation.surface: Wondering which tongue is spoken at a Londoner's party.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, famous for dropping h.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely used in India.

clue.text: Police programme understands the way to …

parts.note: to cop is slang for to catch or grasp
how means the way to do something

explanation.surface: A TV crime drama knows how to lead into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop show is a television drama about police officers solving crimes.

clue.text: … confound American criminal with Roman law

parts.note: perp is US slang for perpetrator
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A US crook baffles police by citing ancient Roman law.
explanation.definitionFit: To perplex is to puzzle or bewilder someone completely.
